newsitem.title: CHINA: China car emission plan seen boosting exports.
newsitem.headline: China car emission plan seen boosting exports.

text.p: China could export locally-made cars to other Asian nations if it follows up a plan to phase out leaded petrol with measures to fit its vehicles with technology to reduce emissions, officials said on Wednesday.

China was considering adopting European emission standards that would require the use of catalytic converters to cut air pollution, said James Rosenstein, spokesman for the European Automobile Manufacturers Association.
No cars now made in China were fitted with converters because such devices required the use of unleaded petrol, which is unavailable in China, said Klaus Schindler, an official with Volkswagen AG.
China has pledged to phase out the use of leaded petrol in major cities, starting with Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou, by the year 2000.
Use of the converters would open up markets in countries with more stringent air quality standards such as Singapore and Malaysia, Schindler told a news briefing.

Schindler said it would be no problem for Volkswagen's China units -- which include Santana production in Shanghai and Jetta and Audi production in Changchun -- to fit their vehicles with the converters.
Association officials had also advised Chinese authorities on how to implement the technology through measures such as tax breaks on purchases of cars made with the converters, he said.
"It's not enough to introduce the technology and unleaded gasoline, people have to buy the technology," Rosenstein said.

Volkswagen and other companies also wanted to introduce lower-emission diesel cars to the Chinese market but the absence of diesel fuel for passengers cars in China had made this impossible for now, Schindler said.
